name: Estelle
role: folk dancer, Live Oak Park Social Hall, North Berkeley; created at the table in Ep 6
disposition: warm, direct, entirely unbothered; adopts the worst dancer in the room on principle
description: Early eighties and the best mover on that floor. Broomstick skirt, silver bracelets you hear before you see her. She has been coming close to the beginning of the dance, which puts her at about fifty when it started. She drafted {{pc:1}} on sight — he was the visible newcomer and he was wearing a very good jacket — and she came back every round or two to check on him, including while he was under the stage with the sound system.
voice: Says the true thing pleasantly and does not soften it. Does not ask twice. Treats being busy as a temporary condition she is happy to wait out.
signature: The drafting line, on sight: "That's a lovely jacket. It's going to be very warm in about four minutes."
The refusal she does not accept: "You're busy. I'll come back."
Everyone was new once — said as a fact about the room, not as encouragement.
dmNotes:
**HER JOB IS DONE. Do not write her a return.**

**RECATEGORISED 2026-09-06, and the error was ours.** She was **improvised** — the DM asked for a name for a spry dancer in a broomstick skirt who existed for one joke about a jacket, and one was invented mid-session. **She was then given this file with an arc function, lane discipline and a PRIME CALLBACK flag: the treatment an authored noun gets.** Nothing was wrong with the name. **Everything was wrong with the category.** That single miscategorisation put a venue, a trip and a scene on the schedule for a jacket joke. See `../../design/DM-ONLY/authoring-rules.md` §1.

**HER EXIT, and it costs nothing.** She is mentioned once, by somebody else, and never staged. The carrier already exists — **T22 holds two unspent Winnie returns**, one reserved for Rosa's second session. Put her inside it:

> *"Estelle asked after the one in the good jacket. Whether he ever came back."*

**Seven words, inside a scene that already exists.** No venue, no travel, no NPC to run — and it delivers the whole payload the callback wanted: **she remembered him, and she wondered.** It converts a scene into a fact.

**Why not simply delete her:** the dancers were the first NPCs in this campaign who were not load-bearing, and they were the most loved *because* nothing was owed. **That morning is the only evidence the table has that meeting somebody can be its own reward.** Seven words is the highest return-per-word spend available; deleting it silently forfeits the lesson.

**WHAT SHE WAS, for the record.** Early eighties, broomstick skirt, silver bracelets you hear before you see her, the best mover on that floor. **She drafted {{pc:1}} on sight because of his jacket** and kept coming back to check on him. Older than Rosa. The standing refutation of {{pc:2}}'s fall-risk worry — right about the anatomy, wrong about the danger — **which already fired at the table and needs no return to land.**
